changes_vs_current:
Scope: man-made landmarks and monuments only. Natural wonders (Grand Canyon, Niagara Falls, Yellowstone, Everest, Uluru, Victoria Falls) are excluded because National Parks is its own topic and the board is 'landmarks'; they were dropped from every source before ranking. Mount Rushmore counts (carved monument). City districts/parks (Central Park, Las Vegas Strip) excluded; Times Square kept as a named landmark. Merges: Sphinx folded into Pyramids of Giza (alias), Houses of Parliament into Big Ben, Sistine Chapel/Vatican into St. Peter's Basilica, Parthenon into Acropolis.
Computed order (avg position over 8 people sources: YouGov US fame, Facts Institute US searches, AllClear recognition, Generali US want-to-visit, Wikipedia 2025 pageviews, BA UK poll, Instagram hashtags, Hotels.com 2009; missing = list length + 5): 1 Eiffel Tower 2.0, 2 Statue of Liberty 4.38, 3 Taj Mahal 7.38, 4 Empire State Building 9.12, 5 Colosseum 10.75, 6 White House 11.12, 7 Golden Gate Bridge 12.0, 8 Machu Picchu 12.62, 9 Great Wall 12.62, 10 Mount Rushmore 12.88, 11 Stonehenge 13.0, 12 Burj Khalifa 13.88, 13 Big Ben 14.25, 14 Pyramids 14.25, 15 Louvre 15.5, 16 Sagrada Familia 15.62, 17 Christ the Redeemer 17.25, 18 Sydney Opera House 17.25, 19 Leaning Tower of Pisa 17.25, 20 St. Peter's 17.38, 21 Times Square 17.5, 22 Acropolis 18.0, 23 One World Trade Center 18.0, 24 Notre-Dame 19.12, then Hollywood Sign 19.25, Alcatraz 19.5, Brooklyn Bridge 19.5, US Capitol 19.62, Petra 19.75, Hagia Sophia 19.88.
Gut-check moves (gut 12 written before ranking): (1) Great Wall 9 -> 4: penalized only by absence from AllClear's published top 20 (apparently not among its 50 tested) and the short Facts top 10; every source that includes it puts it high (YouGov fame 94%, 10th of 30 and 2nd among non-US sites; Generali 5 of 7; BA 6; Wikipedia 7). (2) Pyramids 14 -> 6: not in YouGov's attraction list at all (absent, not rated low); Generali 3, BA 5, AllClear 9, Wikipedia 11. (3) Big Ben 13 -> 11 and Leaning Tower of Pisa 19 -> 12: also absent from YouGov's list; AllClear recognition puts them 7 and 8 (above Rushmore, Golden Gate, Machu Picchu), BA 2 and 7, Instagram has Big Ben 4. (4) Machu Picchu 8 -> 13 and Stonehenge 11 -> 14 stay just outside the top 12 although in the gut 12: YouGov US fame puts both below Empire State Building and White House (Stonehenge 88%, Machu Picchu 80% vs 96-97%), and AllClear places both below Big Ben and Pisa (10 and 13 vs 7 and 8). (5) Empire State Building (4 -> 7) and White House (6 -> 10) shift down only because gut-check items were inserted above; both stay top 10 on strong US data (YouGov fame 96/97%, US searches 5th/7th of 10). Golden Gate 7 -> 9 and Rushmore stays ~8 for the same reason; Golden Gate above White House per T+L tie-break and Instagram. (6) Burj Khalifa 12 -> 15: its high average comes from global Wikipedia (2nd) and Instagram; US data is weak (YouGov fame 81%, popularity 35%, last of 10 in US searches). (7) Sagrada Familia 16 -> 23: lifted by global Wikipedia (4th) and Hotels.com 2009 global travelers; YouGov US fame is only 47% (last of 30 landmarks), so Americans rarely name it. Louvre 16, Christ the Redeemer 17, Sydney Opera House 18, Times Square 19, St. Peter's 20, Acropolis 21, One WTC 22 follow the computed order. Notre-Dame 24 edges Hollywood Sign (19.25), Alcatraz, Brooklyn Bridge, Capitol by computed average; these US sites are left off, which is the main tail doubt.
confidence: High for 1-2 (Eiffel Tower and Statue of Liberty lead every source). Medium-high for 3-12: membership is solid, internal order rests on mixed sources (global recognition, US fame, US search, a UK poll) plus gut-check moves for Great Wall, Pyramids, Big Ben and Pisa, which are missing from YouGov's attraction list rather than rated low. Medium-low for 13-24: tail mixes global-interest sites (Burj, Sagrada, Acropolis) with US sites; Hollywood Sign, Alcatraz, Brooklyn Bridge, US Capitol, Lincoln Memorial were close misses (computed 25-28). No US general-public 'name a landmark' poll was found; several sources are old (Hotels.com 2009, BA 2015, Instagram 2019) or non-US. Some fetches failed (TravelPulse/Kuoni state map, JetPunk quiz stats, Hilton wish-list survey) and are not cited.
